node.title: Re: ne vs. ! eq
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Precedence. See [doc://perlop#Operator-Precedence-and-Associativity|perlop]: ! $s1 eq $s2 is the same as (!$s1) eq $s2, and not !( $s1 eq $s2 ), as [doc://B::Deparse] will tell you:

$ perl -MO=Deparse,-p -e 'if (! $s1 eq $s2) {}' if (((!$s1) eq $s2)) { (); }

You'll need to write either if ( !( $s1 eq $s2 ) ), if ( not $s1 eq $s2 ), unless ( $s1 eq $s2 ), or of course if ( $s1 ne $s2 ).
